instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a latency-sensitive application in AWS account A and its database in AWS account B, in the us-east-1 Region. Both accounts were created in 2021. The VPCs of the two accounts are connected, and each account creates subnets in its own VPC. The company wants the application instances and the database in the same physical Availability Zone. The engineers in each account choose zones by the names that their own console shows, such as us-east-1a. The company must ensure that both workloads use the same physical zone. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Move the application and the database into one AWS account, so that both workloads see the same zone names for the same physical zones.

options.label: B
options.text: Look up the AZ ID of the database subnet, such as use1-az2, and create the application subnet in the zone with the same AZ ID.

options.label: C
options.text: Create the application subnet in the zone that has the same Availability Zone name, such as us-east-1a, as the database subnet in the other account.

options.label: D
options.text: Open an AWS Support case to ask AWS to map the Availability Zone names of both accounts to the same physical zones.
